text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.

- Zagrebacka Banka says it will cut mandatory deposit, taken as security for housing loans, to 10 from between 30 and 50 percent and improve mortgage terms for all those looking to buy new homes as of January 1, 1997.

- Airbus believe Croatia Airlines chose it for a new aircraft supplier in order to be able to run in the race with Alitalia, Austrian Airlines, Swissair and Lufthansa, as all of them have purchased Airbus planes.
- EBRD expert Denes Bulkai says the EBRD is considering financing the reconstruction of JANAF.

- Dairy tycoon Luka Rajic announces that his Lura group might float its shares on the London bourse in search of investors and capital. Rumours have it that Austrian bank Creditainstalt is interested in buying shares in Lura on behalf of a third party.
- Agriculture and Forestry Minister Matej Jankovic announces farming subsidies from the budget will be increased to 561 from 510 million kuna next year.

- Disciplinary procedure against the dismissed Supreme Court president Krunislav Olujic to commence on December 5 before the State Judicial Council. Meanwhile, Olujic sues the Council president, Ante Potrebica, for libel. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
